subject: cougar mountain lion
title: A Cougar Walked 1,500 Miles From South Dakota to Connecticut

scenes.text: A cougar turned up where none had been confirmed in over a century.
In June 2011, a 140-pound male cougar was hit by an SUV in Milford, Connecticut.
Its DNA matched the cougars of the Black Hills in South Dakota.
Hair, blood and droppings showed it had crossed Minnesota and Wisconsin on the way.
That's about 1,500 miles, more than twice the old record for a cougar.
Most young cougars settle within 100 miles of home. This one just kept walking.

description:
In 2011 a mountain lion appeared in Connecticut, the first confirmed in the state in more than a century.
After it was killed by an SUV in Milford on June 11, DNA tests by the US Forest Service traced the 140-pound young male to the Black Hills of South Dakota, and matched it to hair, blood and scat collected in Minnesota and Wisconsin in 2009 and 2010. Its trip of about 1,500 miles (2,400 km) more than doubled the previous cougar record of 663 miles.
Where do you think it was heading?
first_comment: Trail cameras in Wisconsin caught it on the way, and locals nicknamed it the St. Croix mountain lion. Where was it heading?
